1.subtopic: Viscosity, Stokes' Law, Terminal Velocity, and Reynolds
1.solution: Terminal velocity \(v_T \propto r^2\), so \(\frac{r_1^2}{r_2^2} = \frac{v_{T_1}}{v_{T_2}} = \frac{9}{4}\), giving \(\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{3}{2}\). Volume \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), so \(\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}\).

2.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
2.solution: Since \(V_L = V_C = 100\,V\), the inductive and capacitive voltages cancel and the circuit behaves purely resistively (it is at resonance). The full source voltage appears across \(R\), so \(V_R = 300\,V\). The ammeter reads \(I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{300}{50} = 6\,A\).

3.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
3.solution: With \(\omega_0 = 0\), \(\theta = \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2\). In the first 2 s: \(\theta_1 = \frac{1}{2}\alpha(2)^2 = 2\alpha\). In the first 4 s total: \(\theta_{total} = \frac{1}{2}\alpha(4)^2 = 8\alpha\). So in the next 2 s: \(\theta_2 = 8\alpha - 2\alpha = 6\alpha\). Hence \(\theta_1 : \theta_2 = 2\alpha : 6\alpha = 1 : 3\).

4.solution: Density \(\rho = \frac{m}{l^3}\), so the fractional error is \(\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 3\frac{\Delta l}{l}\). Substituting: \(\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = 5\% + 3 \times 6\% = 23\%\).

5.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
5.solution: Comparing \(x = 3 \times 10^{-3}\cos 2\pi t\) with \(x = A\cos(\omega t)\), \(\omega = 2\pi\), so \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 1\,s\). The cosine form means the particle starts at the extreme position. Speed is maximum at the mean position, reached for the first time after a quarter period, i.e. \(\frac{T}{4} = \frac{1}{4}\,s\).

6.subtopic: Kinetic Theory — Pressure, RMS Speed, and Temperature
6.solution: The r.m.s. speed \(v_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3kT}{m}}\) depends only on temperature. In an isothermal process the temperature is constant, so the r.m.s. velocity remains the same.

8.solution: Unpolarised light through the first polaroid: \(I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}\). Each successive polaroid is at \(30^\circ\), so by Malus' law each multiplies the intensity by \(\cos^2 30^\circ = \frac{3}{4}\). After three more polaroids: \(I_4 = \frac{I_0}{2}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^3 = \frac{I_0}{2} \times \frac{27}{64} = \frac{27 I_0}{128}\).

9.subtopic: Kinematics — Equations of Motion, Free Fall, and Graphs
9.solution: Body B accelerates from rest; when its velocity equals \(u\), \(u = at \Rightarrow t = \frac{u}{a}\). Distance of B: \(s_B = \frac{u^2}{2a}\). Distance of A (constant velocity \(u\)): \(s_A = ut = \frac{u^2}{a}\). Separation \(= s_A - s_B = \frac{u^2}{a} - \frac{u^2}{2a} = \frac{u^2}{2a}\).

10.solution: Angular momentum \(L = \frac{nh}{2\pi} \propto n\). Orbital velocity \(v_n = \frac{Ze^2}{2\varepsilon_0 n h} \propto \frac{1}{n}\). Therefore \(\frac{L}{v_n} \propto \frac{n}{1/n} = n^2\).

12.solution: \(\alpha = \frac{I_C}{I_E} = 0.9\) (since 90% of emitted electrons reach the collector). Then \(\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha} = \frac{0.9}{0.1} = 9\). So \(\alpha = 0.9,\ \beta = 9\).

13.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
13.solution: Open-pipe first overtone (2nd harmonic): \(n_1 = \frac{v}{L}\). Closed-pipe first overtone (3rd harmonic): \(n_1' = \frac{3v}{4L}\). Beats: \(n_1 - n_1' = \frac{v}{L} - \frac{3v}{4L} = \frac{v}{4L} = 3 \Rightarrow \frac{v}{L} = 12\). When open length becomes \(\frac{L}{3}\): fundamental \(= \frac{v}{2(L/3)} = \frac{3v}{2L}\). When closed length becomes \(3L\): fundamental \(= \frac{v}{4(3L)} = \frac{v}{12L}\). New beats \(= \frac{3v}{2L} - \frac{v}{12L} = \frac{18v - v}{12L} = \frac{17}{12}\cdot\frac{v}{L} = \frac{17}{12}\times 12 = 17\).

14.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
14.solution: The graph plots radiant power (intensity) against wavelength for a black body. The area under the curve is the total radiant power summed over all wavelengths, i.e. the total energy emitted per unit time per unit area by the black body at all wavelengths.

15.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
15.solution: Maximum current occurs at resonance, where \(X_L = X_C\) and \(C = \frac{1}{\omega^2 L}\). Here \(\omega = 2\pi f = 100\pi\), so \(\omega^2 = (100\pi)^2 = 10^4 \times 10 = 10^5\) (using \(\pi^2 = 10\)). Then \(C = \frac{1}{10^5 \times 2.5} = 4 \times 10^{-6}\,F = 4\,\mu F\). Maximum current \(I_{max} = \frac{V_0}{R} = \frac{230}{11.5} = 20\,A\).

16.subtopic: Satellites, Orbital Motion, and Kepler's Laws
16.solution: By Kepler's third law \(T^2 \propto r^3\). With \(r_2 = \frac{r_1}{4}\): \(\frac{T_2^2}{T_1^2} = \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{64}\), so \(\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{1}{8}\). Hence \(T_2 = \frac{24}{8} = 3\) hours.

17.solution: At the extreme, the bob is at height \(h = L(1-\cos\theta) = 2L\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\). At the mean position, energy conservation gives \(\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh\), so \(v = 2\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\sqrt{gL}\). The maximum induced emf (at the lowest point) is \(\varepsilon_{max} = BLv = 2BL\sqrt{gL}\,\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\).

18.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
18.solution: In a cyclic process the system returns to its initial state, so \(\Delta U = 0\). By the first law \(Q = \Delta U + W = W\). Thus the work done by the system equals the heat given to the system.

19.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
19.solution: By Newton's law of cooling \(\left|\frac{dT}{dt}\right| = k(T - \theta_0)\). So \(1.5 = k(80 - \theta_0)\) and \(0.3 = k(40 - \theta_0)\). Dividing: \(\frac{1.5}{0.3} = \frac{80 - \theta_0}{40 - \theta_0} \Rightarrow 5(40 - \theta_0) = 80 - \theta_0 \Rightarrow 200 - 5\theta_0 = 80 - \theta_0 \Rightarrow 4\theta_0 = 120 \Rightarrow \theta_0 = 30^\circ C\).

20.solution: Inputs A and B each pass through a NOT gate giving \(\overline{A}\) and \(\overline{B}\), which then feed a NAND gate: \(Y = \overline{\overline{A}\cdot\overline{B}}\). By De Morgan's law \(\overline{\overline{A}\cdot\overline{B}} = A + B\). This is the OR gate.

21.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
21.solution: Acceleration \(\overrightarrow{a} = \frac{\overrightarrow{F}}{m} = \frac{4\widehat{i} - 2\widehat{j} + 3\widehat{k}}{5}\). Starting from rest, after \(t = 10\,s\): \(\overrightarrow{v} = \overrightarrow{a}t = 8\widehat{i} - 4\widehat{j} + 6\widehat{k}\). Magnitude \(|\overrightarrow{v}| = \sqrt{8^2 + (-4)^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 16 + 36} = \sqrt{116} = 2\sqrt{29}\,m/s\).

22.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
22.solution: For a closed pipe the \(n^{th}\) overtone is \(f = (2n+1)\frac{v}{4L}\). For an open pipe the \(n^{th}\) overtone is \(f' = (n+1)\frac{v}{2L}\). Their ratio \(\frac{f}{f'} = \frac{(2n+1)v/4L}{(n+1)v/2L} = \frac{2n+1}{2(n+1)}\).

23.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
23.solution: Impedance \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + (3R - R)^2} = \sqrt{5}\,R\). The rms current \(I_{rms} = \frac{E_0/\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}R}\). Average power \(P = I_{rms}^2 R = \frac{E_0^2/2}{5R^2}\cdot R = \frac{E_0^2}{10R}\).

24.solution: Doubling the diameter increases volume \(2^3 = 8\) times. At constant temperature, Boyle's law gives \(P_{bottom}\,V = P_{surface}\,(8V)\), so \(P_{bottom} = 8 P_{surface}\). Expressing pressures as water columns with relative density of mercury \(\rho\): \(P_{surface} = \rho h\) and \(P_{bottom} = \rho h + d\) (where \(d\) is the depth in water). Thus \(8\rho h = \rho h + d \Rightarrow d = 7\rho h\).

25.solution: For a receding source the Doppler shift gives \(\frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} = \frac{v}{c}\). So \(v = \frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda}c = \frac{0.02}{100}\times 3 \times 10^8 = 6 \times 10^4\,m/s = 60\,km/s\).

26.solution: With two parallel dielectric layers each of thickness \(\frac{d}{2}\), the slabs are effectively in series. The equivalent dielectric constant is \(K_{eq} = \frac{2K_1 K_2}{K_1 + K_2}\), so \(C_K = K_{eq}\,C_P\). Therefore \(\frac{C_P}{C_K} = \frac{1}{K_{eq}} = \frac{K_1 + K_2}{2K_1 K_2}\).

27.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
27.solution: \(\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T\). Using \(C_v = \frac{R}{\gamma - 1}\), \(\Delta U = \frac{nR\Delta T}{\gamma - 1}\). At constant pressure \(P\Delta V = nR\Delta T\), so \(\Delta U = \frac{P\Delta V}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{P(2V - V)}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{PV}{\gamma - 1}\).

28.solution: The potential gradient is \(k = \frac{V}{L}\). Increasing the wire length \(L\) (with \(V\) constant) decreases the potential gradient. Since the balancing length is \(l = \frac{\text{emf}}{k}\), a smaller gradient gives a larger balancing length, so the null point is obtained at a larger distance.

29.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
29.stemOverride: A solid sphere rolling without friction on a horizontal surface with a constant speed of \(2\,m/s\), rolls up on an inclined ramp which is inclined at \(30^{\circ}\). The maximum distance travelled by the sphere on the inclined ramp is (acceleration due to gravity \(g = 10\,m/s^{2}, \sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\))
29.solution: Total kinetic energy of a rolling solid sphere \(= \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{5}mv^2 = \frac{7}{10}mv^2\). At maximum height \(\frac{7}{10}mv^2 = mgh\), so \(h = \frac{7v^2}{10g} = \frac{7 \times 4}{100} = 0.28\,m\). Distance along the incline \(d = \frac{h}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{0.28}{0.5} = 0.56\,m = 56\,cm\).

30.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
30.solution: Fringe width \(\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}\), so \(\Delta\beta = \frac{\lambda\,\Delta D}{d}\) and \(\Delta D = \frac{\Delta\beta\, d}{\lambda} = \frac{3 \times 10^{-5} \times 10^{-3}}{600 \times 10^{-9}} = 5\,cm\). Moving the screen away by 5 cm increases the fringe width by this amount; moving it towards the slits by 5 cm decreases it by the same amount. Hence both (A) and (B) give the required change.

31.subtopic: Prism — Deviation, Dispersion, and Refractive Index
31.solution: For the doublet \(P = P_{convex} + P_{concave}\), so \(P_{concave} = 2 - 5 = -3\,D\). Achromatism requires \(\frac{\omega_1}{f_1} + \frac{\omega_2}{f_2} = 0\), i.e. \(\frac{\omega_{convex}}{\omega_{concave}} = -\frac{f_{convex}}{f_{concave}} = -\frac{P_{concave}}{P_{convex}} = -\frac{-3}{5} = \frac{3}{5}\). The ratio is \(3:5\).
31.note: Achromatic-doublet/dispersion question; filed under Prism — Deviation, Dispersion, and Refractive Index as the closest dispersion subtopic (no dedicated achromatic-lens subtopic).

32.subtopic: Magnetic Dipole Moment and Bar Magnet
32.solution: With \(M_A = 2M_B\): like poles together give \(M = M_A + M_B = 3M_B\); unlike poles together give \(M = M_A - M_B = M_B\). Period \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{I}{MB_H}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\). So \(\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{unlike}}{M_{like}}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_B}{3M_B}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). Thus \(T_1 : T_2 = 1 : \sqrt{3}\).

33.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
33.solution: For SHM, \(a = \omega^2 x\), so \(a_1 + a_2 = \omega^2(x_1 + x_2)\). Also \(V^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)\), giving \(V_2^2 - V_1^2 = \omega^2(x_1^2 - x_2^2) = \omega^2(x_1 - x_2)(x_1 + x_2)\). Dividing, \(V_2^2 - V_1^2 = (x_1 - x_2)(a_1 + a_2)\). Since \(a_1 < a_2\) (so \(x_1 < x_2\)), the distance between positions is \(|x_2 - x_1| = \frac{V_1^2 - V_2^2}{a_1 + a_2}\).

34.solution: For an ideal transformer the power is conserved: \(P = V_S I_S\). So \(I_S = \frac{P}{V_S} = \frac{4.4 \times 10^3}{3.3 \times 10^3} = \frac{4}{3}\,A\).

36.solution: By Rydberg's formula \(\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)\). Second excited state to first excited state: \(n_2 = 3, n_1 = 2\), \(\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right) = R\cdot\frac{5}{36}\). Third excited state to second orbit: \(n_2 = 4, n_1 = 2\), \(\frac{1}{\lambda_0} = R\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16}\right) = R\cdot\frac{3}{16}\). So \(\frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda} = \frac{5/36}{3/16} = \frac{5}{36}\times\frac{16}{3} = \frac{20}{27}\), i.e. \(\lambda_0 = \frac{20\lambda}{27}\), giving \(x = 27\).

37.solution: By Gauss' law the total flux through the closed cylinder is \(\phi_A + \phi_B + \phi_C = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\). By symmetry the flux through the two plane ends is equal, \(\phi_A = \phi_B\). With \(\phi_C = \phi\): \(2\phi_A + \phi = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\), so \(\phi_A = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0} - \phi\right)\).

38.solution: For a spring-mass system \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}\), so \(T \propto \sqrt{m}\). Then \(\frac{T'}{T} = \sqrt{\frac{x+Y}{x}} = \frac{4}{3}\), giving \(\frac{x+Y}{x} = \frac{16}{9}\), so \(1 + \frac{Y}{x} = \frac{16}{9}\) and \(\frac{Y}{x} = \frac{7}{9}\), i.e. \(7:9\).

40.solution: For a rolling disc, total KE \(= \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}mR^2\right)\frac{v^2}{R^2} = \frac{3}{4}mv^2 = mgh\), so \(mv^2 = \frac{4}{3}mgh\). Rotational KE \(= \frac{1}{4}mv^2 = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{3}mgh = \frac{mgh}{3}\).

41.solution: Wire fundamental matches closed-pipe fundamental: \(\frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}} = \frac{v}{4L}\). After increasing tension by 8 N, wire matches the closed-pipe first overtone: \(\frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T+8}{m}} = \frac{3v}{4L}\). 42.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
42.solution: The \(100\,\Omega\) resistor carries the total current from the 6 V source. Diode \(D_1\) is reverse biased, while \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are forward biased (each with forward resistance \(40\,\Omega\)). The conducting branches are \(D_2 + 60\,\Omega = 100\,\Omega\) and \(D_3 + 160\,\Omega = 200\,\Omega\), in parallel: \(\frac{100 \times 200}{300} = \frac{200}{3}\,\Omega\). Total resistance \(R = 100 + \frac{200}{3} = \frac{500}{3}\,\Omega\). Current \(I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{6}{500/3} = \frac{18}{500} = 0.036\,A = 36\,mA\).

43.solution: Each shell of radius \(R\) and surface charge density \(\pm\sigma\) carries charge \(Q = 4\pi R^2\sigma\). The potential at the innermost shell A is the sum of contributions: from A (at its own surface) \(\frac{a\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\); from B \(\frac{-b\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\); from C \(\frac{c\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\). Each is computed as \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{Q}{R_{shell}}\) using the shell's own radius. Thus \(V_A = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(a - b + c)\).

46.solution: Volume conservation: \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 512\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), so \(R = 8r\). Surface energy \(\propto\) area. Total area of droplets \(= 512(4\pi r^2) = 512\cdot 4\pi\left(\frac{R}{8}\right)^2 = 8(4\pi R^2)\). So \(\frac{E_2}{E_1} = 8\), giving \(E_2 = 8E\).

47.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
47.solution: Ray AB (reflected at the top surface) has intensity \(I_1 = \frac{1}{4}I\). The other ray AB' is transmitted at A (\(\frac{3}{4}I\)), reflected at the bottom surface (\(\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{3}{4}I = \frac{3}{16}I\)), then transmitted out at A' (\(\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{3}{16}I = \frac{9}{64}I\)). Since \(I \propto A^2\): \(A_1 = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{I} = \frac{4}{8}\sqrt{I}\), \(A_2 = \frac{3}{8}\sqrt{I}\). So \(\frac{I_{max}}{I_{min}} = \left(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{7/8}{1/8}\right)^2 = 49\), i.e. \(49:1\).

48.solution: The curved part QRS is a three-quarter circle subtending \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) at the centre O, contributing \(B_1 = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I}{r}\cdot\frac{3\pi}{2}\). The straight wire PQ lies along the line through O, so its perpendicular distance from O is zero and it contributes nothing. The straight wire ST is a semi-infinite wire whose perpendicular foot is at S (distance r from O), contributing \(B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\). All contributions are along \(+\widehat{k}\) (out of the plane), giving \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\left(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 1\right)\widehat{k}\).

49.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
49.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
49.solution: With negligible work function, the photoelectron's kinetic energy \(K = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\). The de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda_1 = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m\,hc/\lambda}} = \frac{h\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{2mhc}}\). So \(\lambda_1^2 = \frac{h^2\lambda}{2mhc}\) and \(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_1^2} = \frac{2mhc}{h^2} = \frac{2mc}{h}\). Thus \(\lambda : \lambda_1^2 = 2mc : h\).

58.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
58.solution: Rate \(= k[A]^{x}\). Increasing \([A]\) tenfold multiplies the rate by \(10^{x}\). Given the rate increases 100 times: \(10^{x} = 100 \Rightarrow x = 2\). Order \(= 2\).

59.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
59.solution: Terbium (Tb, Z = 65) has the configuration \([Xe]4f^{9}6s^{2}\). On forming \(Tb^{4+}\) it loses 4 electrons to give a half-filled, stable \(4f^{7}\) configuration. Hence Tb exhibits the +4 state with an \(f^{7}\) configuration.

60.solution: A salt that turns red litmus blue gives a basic solution. KCN is the salt of a strong base (KOH) and a weak acid (HCN); it hydrolyses to give a basic solution. NaNO3, NaCl and KCl are salts of strong acid and strong base and are neutral.

61.solution: Moles: \(n_{N_{2}} = 28/28 = 1\), \(n_{He} = 8/4 = 2\), \(n_{Ne} = 40/20 = 2\); total \(= 5\ \text{mol}\).\nMole fraction \(x_{N_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2\).\nPartial pressure \(P_{N_{2}} = x_{N_{2}} \times P_{\text{total}} = 0.2 \times 20 = 4\ \text{bar}\).

62.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
62.solution: Counting electrons in bonding molecular orbitals: \(N_{2}\) has 10 bonding electrons and \(O_{2}\) also has 10 bonding electrons. They are equal, so the statement that \(N_{2}\) has MORE bonding electrons than \(O_{2}\) is incorrect. (\(O_{2}\) is less stable only because it has more antibonding electrons.) The other statements are correct: \(N_{2}\) is more stable than \(O_{2}\), its bond order is 3, and it is diamagnetic.

63.solution: Boiling points of hydrogen halides: HF is highest due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding (293 K). For the rest the boiling point rises with molecular size: HI (238 K) > HBr (206 K) > HCl (189 K). Overall: \(HF > HI > HBr > HCl\).

64.solution: Glucose \(C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}\) has 6 carbon atoms per molecule.\nCarbon atoms \(= 0.35 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6 = 1.264 \times 10^{24}\).

65.solution: For the non-electrolyte: \(\Delta T_{b} = K_{b}\,m = x\ \text{K}\).\n\(AlCl_{3}\) dissociates: \(AlCl_{3} \to Al^{3+} + 3Cl^{-}\), giving 4 particles, so van't Hoff factor \(i = 4\).\nHence \(\Delta T_{b} = i \times K_{b}\,m = 4x\ \text{K}\).

66.solution: In a dry (Leclanche) cell the positive electrode (cathode) is the site of reduction: \(2MnO_{2(s)} + 2NH_{4}^{+} + 2e^{-} \to Mn_{2}O_{3(s)} + 2NH_{3} + H_{2}O\). Thus \(MnO_{2}\) (Mn in +4) is reduced to \(Mn_{2}O_{3}\) (Mn in +3).

69.solution: Quicklime is calcium oxide (CaO), obtained by thermal decomposition (calcination) of calcium carbonate: \(CaCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO + CO_{2}\).

71.solution: Silver nanoparticles act as a highly effective antibacterial disinfectant and are used to remove E. coli bacteria from water.

72.solution: The reaction \(NO_{2} + NO_{2} \to 2NO + O_{2}\) is an elementary reaction in which two \(NO_{2}\) molecules collide, so molecularity \(= 2\). For an elementary reaction the order equals the molecularity, so order \(= 2\).

74.solution: All four options are isomeric butanols \((C_{4}H_{9}OH)\). Boiling point decreases with increased branching (more compact, smaller surface area, weaker van der Waals forces). The most branched isomer, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol, option D), has the lowest boiling point.

75.solution: In \(BrF_{5}\) the central Br has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (\(sp^{3}d^{2}\), octahedral electron geometry). With one lone pair the molecular shape is square pyramidal.

76.solution: Cleavage of the \(C-X\) bond in haloarenes (aromatic nucleophilic substitution) is accelerated by electron-withdrawing \(-NO_{2}\) groups at the ortho/para positions. More \(-NO_{2}\) groups means greater reactivity. Compound III (2,4,6-trinitro) is most reactive, followed by the dinitro/nitro structures: \(III > II > I\).

81.solution: The pyrimidine ring of nucleic acid bases has two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3 of the six-membered ring.

82.solution: The methoxy (\(-OCH_{3}\)) group is an activating, ortho/para-directing substituent. Bromination of anisole with \(Br_{2}\) in acetic acid (mild, monobromination) gives predominantly the para product, p-bromoanisole (the bulky ortho position is less favoured).

84.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
84.solution: Alkyl groups release electrons (+I effect), stabilizing the positive charge on the nitrogen of the protonated species. More alkyl groups means greater stabilization: \(NH_{4}^{+} < RNH_{3}^{+} < R_{2}NH_{2}^{+} < R_{3}NH^{+}\). The trialkyl-substituted cation \(R_{3}NH^{+}\) is most stable.

87.solution: Nernst equation: \(E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log_{10}\dfrac{[Cd^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}\).\nWith \([Cd^{2+}] = 10[Cu^{2+}]\): \(E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log_{10}10 = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - 0.0296\ \text{V}\).\nSo \(E_{\text{cell}}\) is less than \(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}\) by 0.0296 V.

90.solution: Magnetic moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\) increases with the number of unpaired electrons. \(Cu^{2+}\) is \(3d^{9}\) (1 unpaired, \(\mu = 1.73\) BM); \(Cr^{3+}\ 3d^{3}\) and \(Co^{2+}\ 3d^{7}\) have 3 unpaired; \(Fe^{2+}\ 3d^{6}\) has 4 unpaired. \(Cu^{2+}\) has the least magnetic moment.

91.solution: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) contains an ESTER linkage (and a carboxylic acid group), not an amide linkage. So the statement 'It contains amide linkage' is false. The other statements (obtained from salicylic acid, fewer side effects than salicylic acid, stomach-irritating) are true.

92.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
92.solution: Boiling point of aldehydes increases with molecular weight (stronger van der Waals forces). Valeraldehyde (pentanal, \(C_{4}H_{9}CHO\)) is the largest and has the highest boiling point.

93.solution: An n-type semiconductor is formed by doping a Group 14 element (Ge) with a Group 15 element that has an extra valence electron. Among the options, arsenic (As) is the Group 15 dopant; B, In and Ga are Group 13 (p-type dopants).

94.solution: Entropy decreases when randomness decreases, i.e. when going from a more disordered to a more ordered state. Condensation of a gas to a liquid, \(H_{2}O_{(g)} \to H_{2}O_{(l)}\), decreases entropy. The other options (solid to liquid/gas, liquid to gas) all increase entropy.

95.solution: The statement that no two electrons in an atom can have an identical set of four quantum numbers is Pauli's exclusion principle.

96.solution: Diborane \((B_{2}H_{6})\) selectively reduces the carboxylic acid group \(-COOH\) to a primary alcohol. It does not reduce esters \((-COOR)\), nitro groups \((-NO_{2})\) or halides \((-X)\) under the same conditions.
